Morgan (Support): FYI — Aisha reports that Console CSV export for account `ac-72ef` returns an empty file or header-only when selecting a long custom range (>90d). Said it happens in Chrome + Excel on Windows. URL: https://app.redwood.example/exports/eyJ...

Aisha (Customer): Repro steps I did:
1) Console -> Analytics -> Exports -> Custom range 2024-01-01 -> 2024-04-10
2) Click Export -> Download from notifications -> file is 0 bytes or only contains header row.
3) I tried direct presigned link in incognito, got a download that opens as gibberish in Excel.

Sample quick check I ran in terminal:
```
$ curl -I "https://s3-presigned.example/abc123"
HTTP/1.1 200 OK
Content-Type: application/octet-stream
Content-Encoding: gzip
Content-Length: 0
Content-Disposition: attachment; filename=export.csv
```

Morgan (Support): Thanks, that helps. Can you paste the full presigned URL (pm if sensitive) and browser devtools network HAR? Also which org/plan so we can prioritize.

Priya (SRE): @Morgan can you confirm if the S3 object shows bytes in our backend put logs? If Content-Length is 0 at GET time but PUT showed N bytes, might be gzip/content-encoding mismatch or a streaming/upload truncation.

Ethan (Eng-Infra): Looking at last week's streaming change: we started piping CSV -> gzip stream -> multipart upload and set `Content-Encoding: gzip` on the S3 object, but our presigned GET generator didn't include `response-content-encoding` or strip headers. Some browsers/Excel OLE expect a UTF-8 BOM or plain `text/csv` and will mis-detect. That could produce the "looks empty" symptom when Excel can't parse compressed bytes. Also saw one bug where intermediate buffer zeroed out when chunked upload raced with metadata update — possible race that results in 0-length object in S3 index even though parts present.

Ethan (Eng-Infra): Quick log snippet from the put job: 
```
[2026-03-16T14:02:11Z] export-upload: upload_id=exp-9a4f parts=12 total_bytes=12345678 meta_set=true content_encoding=gzip
[2026-03-16T14:02:12Z] export-upload: finalize: upload_id=exp-9a4f status=complete
[2026-03-16T14:02:12Z] s3-metadata: object_size=0  <-- suspicious
```

Carlos (Product): We're getting 2 other support tickets about the same thing from enterprise customers. This likely needs a fast rollback or a hotfix. Short-term workaround OK?

Ethan (Eng-Infra): Workarounds:
- Customer can fetch the object via our API endpoint (/v1/exports/<id>/raw) which streams decompressed CSV properly.
- Or download and run `gunzip -c export.csv > fixed.csv` (if they get bytes but Excel shows garbage).
- We can also force presigned link to set `response-content-disposition=attachment; filename=export.csv` and `response-content-type=text/csv; charset=utf-8` which helps some clients.

Priya (SRE): We should mark this P1 for exports during peak and do a rollback of the streaming change if we see more than 5% error rate in the next hour. Also collect HAR from affected users so we can reproduce client behavior in Windows+Excel.

Morgan (Support): I'll send the API workaround to the customer and ask them to confirm. @Aisha can you try the API endpoint and respond here?

Aisha (Customer): Tried the API `/v1/exports/eyJ.../raw` — that streamed fine and Excel opened the file with the rows intact. Thanks, that's a workable workaround for now. Please let me know when it's fixed. :pray:

Ethan (Eng-Infra): Plan: revert the risky bits and/or patch. I opened PR https://git.example/r/redwood/infra/merge_requests/724 with branch `fix/streaming-s3-headers` — changes: only set `Content-Encoding: gzip` if the object store can serve compressed content with proper headers on GET; ensure we set `Content-Type: text/csv; charset=utf-8` and add UTF-8 BOM for Excel compatibility; add atomic finalize step to avoid metadata/race. Added unit + integration tests for presigned URLs. Commit: 4f7a9b2

Priya (SRE): Nice. Add an e2e that uploads a gzip object and then fetches via presigned GET from a Windows worker in CI. Also capture performance regression risk.

deploy-bot: Deployed branch `fix/streaming-s3-headers` to staging at 2026-03-16T16:45:01Z :rocket:

Ethan (Eng-Infra): Will canary to 10% prod in 2h, monitor `export.download.errors` and `export.download.zero_byte_count`. Roll back if error rate spikes or we see >1% 0-byte downloads.

Carlos (Product): Communicated ETA to affected customers: hotfix rolling, expected prod deploy in ~4h.

Morgan (Support): Customer confirmed API workaround. I'll follow up with them post-deploy and close once we verify. Thanks team :thumbsup:

Aisha (Customer): Thanks everyone — appreciate the fast response.

Ethan (Eng-Infra): Follow-up note: after deploy we observed the previously empty objects restored to correct size for new exports. We did a backfill script for 3 affected exports to regenerate their CSVs.

Morgan (Support): Closing thread — will reopen if customer reports persistent issues. :white_check_mark:
